- When sentiment is consistently bullish (high sentiment levels) and news volume is stable, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns bearish mid-period, model lags in adjusting downward — apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- When sentiment volatility is high (frequent changes), model exhibits erratic behavior — smooth forecasts using moving average of last 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price returns to prior range), model overreacts — dampen forecast by 10–15% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- In low-news periods (news volume = 0), model tends to drift — anchor forecast to recent 7-day average unless sentiment strongly shifts.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often underreacts — increase forecast slightly to account for sentiment momentum.
